name: ai-context-hub
description: A thin status bar and panel over the aihub CLI: story, branch, pull request, pipeline, review threads, Fabric runs and watch events. Actions open in your chat (Copilot Chat or opencode).

aihub.chatTarget.description: Where actions go. auto: an open opencode terminal if there is one, otherwise Copilot Chat. The text is put in the chat input; you press Enter yourself.

aihub.refreshIntervalSeconds.description: How often the status is refreshed while the window has focus. The window also refreshes when it gets focus and when the git branch changes. No polling while the window is not focused.

aihub.fabric.enabled.description: Show the Fabric section (runs and failures of the branch's feature workspace via aihub fabric). Hidden automatically when the branch has no workspace.

aihub.cliPath.description: The aihub command. Change this only when aihub is not on the PATH.

aihub.timeoutSeconds.description: Time limit for one aihub call.

aihub.chatAgentName.description: The Copilot Chat agent selected when an action opens the chat (installed by aihub skills install). When it is not installed the default agent is used and the install command is offered once.

aihub.chatAgentMode.description: Open Copilot Chat in agent mode, so the slash commands (/pr, /review, ...) of the aihub pack work.

aihub.worktrees.setsRoot.description: Folder that holds the worktree sets (one folder per branch). Empty: C:\git\worktrees on Windows, ~/git/worktrees elsewhere.

aihub.worktrees.repoRoots.description: Folders scanned for repositories when creating a set. Empty: the parent folders of the workspace folders.

aihub.worktrees.scanDepth.description: How many folder levels below each repo root are scanned for repositories.

aihub.worktrees.baseBranches.description: Base branches offered for a new branch in a set.

aihub.performanceLog.enabled.description: Keep a local performance log of what the extension costs: activation per phase, commands, status reads, every child process (git, aihub, az), timers, watchers, notifications, and every 30-60 s the event-loop delay, CPU and memory of the extension host. JSON lines under the extension's global storage (perf/), at most 10 MB per day, 7 days kept, never sent anywhere. No tokens, e-mail addresses or file contents. See AI Context Hub: Show Performance Report.

aihub.performanceAdvisor.notify.description: Check once a day (first 10 minutes after the start) what makes git, node and VS Code slow here (aihub doctor --perf) and offer one finding as a notification: at most one notification a day, each finding at most once. All findings are in AI Context Hub: Performance Advisor.

aihub.performanceAdvisor.adminDryRun.description: Administrator changes of the Performance Advisor (Defender exclusions) only show what would run, without the UAC prompt. For trying it out.

enumDescriptions: One host sample per minute; timers and watchers as counts in the sample.
One host sample every 30 s, plus a line per timer fire and watcher event.
aihub.performanceLog.level.description: How much the performance log keeps.

aihub.worktrees.cleanupReminder.description: Ask to clean up worktrees whose pull request is completed or abandoned, whose story is done, or that are merged (and that have no local work): at most once a week, sooner when three or more can go, never more than once a day. Clean Up Worktrees... always works.

aihub.worktrees.remote.description: Remote used to fetch, sync and push sets.

enumDescriptions: Ask once when you clearly work in another branch of the story than its ★
Move the ★ yourself, with an Undo button
aihub.storyWorktrees.autoMarkCurrent.description: The ★ of a story follows the branch you really work in (saves, edits, focus time, commits; counted locally in story-worktrees.json).

aihub.set.description: Written by aihub into the .code-workspace of a repo set (story, group, branch, mode, repositories); the status bar shows it. Not meant to be edited.

aihub.reposRoot.markdownDescription: The folder with your clones for the repo opener (New Worktree Set, Repositories on a branch). A repository that is not cloned yet is cloned here. Empty: team.yaml `reposRoot`, else the folder the current repository is in.

aiContextHub.sidebarViews.description: Show the Worktree Sets and My Stories views in the Explorer sidebar. Off by default: the title bar buttons (Open Story, Open Repository, Recent) do the same.

enumDescriptions: Ask once per new stand when a repository is behind its target branch (team.yaml, else staging, else main).
Update by itself when there are no conflicts and no uncommitted work in the way; otherwise ask. A line with Undo follows.
Never look at the target branch.
aiContextHub.behindTarget.description: What to do when a repository of the set is behind its target branch. Looking costs one git fetch per repository: when the set opens, after an Update or Push, when the overview menu opens, and when the window gets focus back after 30 minutes.

aiContextHub.openIn.description: Where a set or repository from the buttons opens. An empty window is always reused.

aiContextHub.continueWhereYouWere.description: In a window with no folder, offer to open the set or repository you worked in last.

aiContextHub.pycharmGitExtensionId.description: Extra id of the PyCharm Git extension (publisher.name). Without that extension installed, AI Context Hub shows one status bar item with the story or set of the window; with it, PyCharm Git shows it in the title bar.

enumDescriptions: Show the review comments of the pull requests of the set (or of the open repository) in the editor and as a count in the Explorer.
No review comments in the editor or the Explorer; nothing is read for them.
aiContextHub.prComments.description: Review comments of pull requests in the editor (Reply, Resolve, Apply Suggestion) and as a count in the Explorer. They are read with the pull requests (one aihub call for all of them): when a set opens, when the overview opens, when the window gets focus back after 5 minutes, and on a refresh. Opening a file reads nothing.

aiContextHub.searchWithoutFocus.description: Test windows only: the search of the left menu may read the Azure DevOps list while the window has no focus (a minimised test window). Normally the list is never read without focus.

colors.description: The count of a file or folder in the Explorer with a pull request comment you have not seen yet.
